{{ElectionsAL}}
The '''2026 Alabama gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Alabama]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] senator [[Tommy Tuberville]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former senator [[Doug Jones (politician)|Doug Jones]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Republican incumbent [[Kay Ivey]] is [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] and ineligible to seek a third full consecutive term.

[[Primary elections]] were held on May 19, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alabama Election Cycle Calendar |url=https://www.sos.alabama.gov/sites/default/files/2025-06/Alabama%20Election%20Chart%202026-2036%206.12.2025.pdf |website=Alabama Secretary of State |access-date=21 March 2025}}</ref> This is a rematch of the [[2020 United States Senate election in Alabama|2020 Senate election]], where Tuberville defeated incumbent senator Jones. Democrats have not won a gubernatorial election in Alabama since [[1998 Alabama gubernatorial election|1998]].

===Campaign===
[[Will Boyd]] was the first candidate to enter the race, in June 2025.<ref name="Boyd"/> [[Doug Jones (politician)|Doug Jones]] did not rule out a bid in the same month, while campaigning for a Democrat in a state legislative special election.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Barrett |first1=Anna |title=Doug Jones endorses, plans to campaign for Cullman County Democrat |url=https://alabamareflector.com/2025/07/02/doug-jones-endorses-plans-to-campaign-for-cullman-county-democrat/ |website=Alabama Reflector |access-date=6 February 2026 |date=July 2, 2025}}</ref> He officially launched his campaign in November 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Drew |title=Doug Jones files paperwork to run for Alabama governor 5 years after losing Senate seat to Tommy Tuberville |url=https://www.cbs42.com/news/local/doug-jones-files-paperwork-to-run-for-alabama-governor-5-years-after-losing-senate-seat-to-tommy-tuberville/ |website=CBS 42 |access-date=6 February 2026 |date=November 24, 2025}}</ref> Following reports that Jones would announce a campaign, Boyd's campaign responded by stating that he would not be dropping out of the race.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chitwood |first1=Bill |title=Dr. Will Boyd Responds to Reports of Doug Jones Governors Run |url=https://alpolitics.com/dr-will-boyd-responds-to-reports-of-doug-jones-governors-run/ |website=ALPolitics.com |access-date=6 February 2026 |date=November 23, 2025}}</ref>

Jones has expressed support for a state [[lottery]] in Alabama.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cortes |first1=Tony |title=Doug Jones visits Huntsville, speaks on campaign for governor |url=https://whnt.com/news/alabama-news/doug-jones-visits-huntsville-speaks-on-campaign-for-governor/ |website=WHNT |access-date=6 February 2026 |date=February 1, 2026}}</ref> He has also pledged to remove members of the [[Alabama Public Library Service]] and replace them with nonpartisan members.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Holmes |first1=Jacob |title=Jones vows to remove APLS members if elected governor |url=https://www.alreporter.com/2026/02/09/jones-vows-to-remove-apls-members-if-elected-governor/ |website=Alabama Political Reporter |access-date=9 February 2026 |date=February 9, 2026}}</ref>

== Challenges to Tuberville's eligibility ==
Alabama's governors, unlike its U.S. senators, must satisfy three conditions set out in Article V, Section 117 of the [[Constitution of Alabama]]:<blockquote>The governor and lieutenant governor shall each be at least thirty years of age when elected, and shall have been citizens of the United States ten years and resident citizens of this state at least seven years next before the date of their election.<ref>{{Cite web|title=SECTION 117|url=https://law.justia.com/constitution/alabama/CA-245654.html|access-date=January 30, 2026|website=[[Justia]]}}</ref> </blockquote>Throughout Tuberville's gubernatorial campaign, many have alleged that he does not satisfy the seven-year residency condition, which would render him ineligible to hold the office.

=== Background ===
[[File:Map of Alabama and Florida with Lee County, AL and Walton County, FL highlighted.png|thumb|Tuberville owns residences in Lee County, Alabama, and Walton County, Florida.]]
Tuberville is originally from Arkansas. In addition to his 9-year tenure at [[Auburn University]] in Alabama, Tuberville's football coaching career variously placed him in Florida, Mississippi, Texas, and Ohio.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brassil |first=Gillian R. |date=2020-07-15 |title=Tuberville Advances: Will Alabama Send an Auburn Coach to the Senate? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/15/sports/tommy-tuberville-alabama-auburn.html |access-date=2026-07-09 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In July 2017, having retired from coaching and joined [[ESPN]] as an analyst, Tuberville recorded a promotional video at his residence in [[Santa Rosa Beach, Florida]], in which he says, "Six months ago, after 40 years of coaching football, I hung up my whistle and moved to Santa Rosa Beach, Florida, with the white sands and the blue water. What a great place to live."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Volner |first=Derek |date=2017-07-19 |title=Greetings from the beach: New ESPN, ABC CFB analyst Tommy Tuberville |url=https://www.espnfrontrow.com/2017/07/greetings-beach-new-espn-abc-cfb-analyst-tommy-tuberville/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=ESPN Front Row |language=en-US}}</ref> Tuberville purchased the 4,000-square-foot Florida residence through an [[Limited liability company|LLC]] in 2004,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hakim |first=Danny |date=2020-10-12 |title=Tommy Tuberville’s Financial Fumbles |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/10/12/us/elections/senate-alabama-tuberville-jones.html |access-date=2026-07-09 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> and its value was estimated at $5.6 million in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Press |first=Associated |date=2026-06-14 |title=Tuberville residency hearing today in Hoover |url=https://aldailynews.com/tuberville-residency-hearing-today-in-hoover/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref>

In March 2017, Tuberville filed preliminary paperwork to run for governor of Alabama in the [[2018 Alabama gubernatorial election|2018 election]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stevens |first=Matthew |title=Tuberville files paperwork & receives $100K loan for potential governor run |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/news/2017/03/31/tuberville-files-paperwork-receives-100k-loan-potential-governor-run/99890632/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Montgomery Advertiser |language=en-US}}</ref> but he withdrew less than a month later, citing the seven-year residency requirement as a concern.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapp |first=Timothy |title=Former Auburn HC Tommy Tuberville Announces He Will Not Run for Alabama Governor |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2705689-former-auburn-hc-tommy-tuberville-announces-he-will-not-run-for-alabama-governor |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref> 

Tuberville was issued an Alabama driver's license in March 2019, shortly before declaring his candidacy in [[2020 United States Senate election in Alabama|the state's 2020 U.S. Senate race]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knowles |first=Sawyer |date=2026-06-15 |title=Alabama Republican Party rules that Tuberville fully meets residency requirements |url=https://256today.com/alabama-republican-party-rules-that-tuberville-fully-meets-residency-requirements/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=256 Today |language=en-US}}</ref> During the campaign, Tuberville claimed that he had moved to Alabama in August of 2018, despite having voted in Florida in the [[2018 United States elections|November 2018 midterm elections]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Dale |date=2019-05-02 |title=Tuberville moved to Alabama to run for Senate in August 2018 -- but voted in Florida in last November's election |url=https://yellowhammernews.com/tuberville-moved-to-alabama-to-run-for-senate-in-august-2018-but-voted-in-florida-in-last-novembers-election/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Yellowhammer News |language=en-US}}</ref> Tuberville cited a 1,551-square-foot home on Cherry Street in [[Auburn, Alabama]], as his primary residence.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=jsharp@al.com |first=John Sharp {{!}} |date=2025-03-26 |title=Tommy Tuberville not the first to raise election residency questions: Do Alabama voters care? |url=https://www.al.com/politics/2025/03/tommy-tuberville-not-the-first-to-raise-election-residency-questions-do-alabama-voters-care.html |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=al |language=en}}</ref> The home was purchased under the names of Tuberville's wife and son in March 2017,<ref name=":0" /> and they claimed a [[homestead exemption]] in October 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sell |first=Mary |date=2025-04-29 |title=Tax records show Tuberville's Auburn homestead exemption since 2018 |url=https://aldailynews.com/tax-records-show-tubervilles-auburn-homestead-exemption-since-2018/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> Tuberville did not appear on the deed for the property himself until 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moon |first=Josh |date=2026-06-17 |title=The first, and most daunting, legal challenge to Tuberville's candidacy has been filed |url=https://www.alreporter.com/2026/06/17/the-first-and-most-daunting-legal-challenge-to-tubervilles-candidacy-has-been-filed/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Political Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref>

During the 2020 Republican primary for U.S. Senate, Republican opponent [[Bradley Byrne]] said of Tuberville, "We don’t like [[Carpetbagger (politics)|carpetbaggers]] in Alabama,"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Poor |first=Jeff |date=2019-05-04 |title=Byrne on Tuberville's Florida voter registration: 'We don't like carpetbaggers in Alabama' |url=https://yellowhammernews.com/byrne-on-tubervilles-florida-voter-registration-we-dont-like-carpetbaggers-in-alabama/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Yellowhammer News |language=en-US}}</ref> to which Tuberville commented at an August 2019 campaign event, "I’m not an everyday resident of Alabama. [...] I’ve been here most of the last 20 years. I’ve had property. So, you’ll see that on TV – ‘He’s a carpetbagger.’ Yeah, I’m a carpetbagger of this country. I love this country. I love this state. I’m a carpetbagger."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Poor |first=Jeff |date=2019-08-04 |title=Tuberville dings Trump for veterans' health care problems, addresses 'carpetbagger' label, tax dodging allegations in Shoals appearances |url=https://yellowhammernews.com/tuberville-dings-trump-for-veterans-health-care-problems-addresses-carpetbagger-label-tax-dodging-allegations-in-shoals-appearances/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Yellowhammer News |language=en-US}}</ref> Republican primary opponent [[Jeff Sessions]] commissioned advertisements labeling Tuberville a "[[Florida Man]]"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lesniewski |first=Niels |date=2020-03-06 |title=Jeff Sessions’ campaign calls Tuberville a ‘Florida man’ |url=https://rollcall.com/2020/03/06/jeff-sessions-campaign-calls-tuberville-a-florida-man/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Roll Call |language=en-US}}</ref> and referred to him as a "tourist from Florida."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-attacks-sessions-ahead-of-senate-primary-runoff |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=www.pbs.org|title=Trump attacks Sessions ahead of Senate primary runoff|date=2020-03-04|last=Chandler|first=Kim}}</ref>

In March 2025, amid speculation that Tuberville would mount a gubernatorial bid, Alabama state senator [[Sam Givhan]], a Republican, expressed concerns about Tuberville's ability to meet the residency requirement, saying during a radio appearance, "Owning a house in Alabama is not enough. You’ve got to live here seven years. [...] So that’s going to be a hurdle."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cason |first=Mike |date=2025-03-18 |title=Can Tuberville run for governor? Alabama Republican questions whether he meets residency requirement |url=https://www.al.com/politics/2025/03/can-tuberville-run-for-governor-alabama-republican-questions-whether-he-meets-residency-requirement.html |access-date=2026-07-15 |website=al |language=en}}</ref>

During Tuberville's tenure as Senator, expense records have shown significant spending on air travel, transportation, and dining in the area near his Florida property.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Britt |first=Bill |date=2025-04-24 |title=Tuberville’s travel trail points to home in Florida, not Alabama |url=https://www.alreporter.com/2025/04/24/tubervilles-travel-trail-points-to-home-in-florida-not-alabama/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Political Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref> In May 2026, speaking to reporters after his induction into the [[Alabama Sports Hall of Fame]], Tuberville said, "I go back to Auburn three or four ball games a year. Actually, I live in Auburn, but living mostly in [[Washington, D.C.|D.C]]., you know, during the week."<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iPdiCn7lUl4 |title=Alabama Sports Hall of Fame interviews: Tommy Tuberville |date=2026-05-08 |last=ABC 33/40 |access-date=2026-07-10 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

=== Challenges from Ken McFeeters ===
[[File:Ken McFeeters - Ralph Chapoco, Alabama Reflector.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Ken McFeeters announced a lawsuit against Tuberville on March 24, 2026.]]
On January 27, 2026, after the filing deadline for the Republican Party primary had passed, Tuberville's gubernatorial primary opponent, Ken McFeeters, submitted a challenge to the [[Alabama Republican Party]], formally alleging that Tuberville did not satisfy the state's residency requirement. McFeeters alleged in his petition that Tuberville primarily resides at his beachfront house in Santa Rosa Beach, Florida.<ref>{{Cite web|author=NBC 15|title=Tuberville's Alabama residency formally challenged by gubernatorial opponent|url=https://mynbc15.com/news/local/tubervilles-alabama-residency-questioned-gop-urged-to-decide-on-eligibility|date=January 27, 2026|access-date=January 30, 2026|website=[[WMTV]]}}</ref> A spokesperson for Tuberville described the challenge as "a ridiculous PR stunt from a desperate candidate,"<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Davis|first1=Kayla|title=Republican candidate challenges Sen. Tommy Tuberville's residency, saying he lives in Florida|url=https://www.wvtm13.com/article/tuberville-mcfeeter-senator-alabama-governor-election/70176207|date=January 28, 2026|access-date=January 30, 2026|website=[[WVTM]]}}</ref> and Tuberville dismissed the allegation, stating, "What a joke. I guess they think, you know, I hadn't done my homework."<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Conlon|first1=Riley|last2=Higdon|first2=Michal|title='What a joke': Sen. Tommy Tuberville dismisses challenge to his Alabama residency|url=https://www.wvtm13.com/article/tuberville-residency-governor-challenge-alabama-florida/70193402|date=January 29, 2026|access-date=January 30, 2026|website=[[WVTM]]}}</ref>

The Alabama Republican Party's 21-member steering committee reviewed the challenge on February 2, 2026, and rejected it, clearing the path for Tuberville to be on the primary ballot.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Marie Fogel |first1=Apryl |title=ALGOP steering committee votes down Tuberville, Wahl ballot challenges |url=https://1819news.com/news/item/algop-steering-committee-votes-down-tuberville-wahl-ballot-challenges |website=1819 News |access-date=2 February 2026 |date=February 2, 2026}}</ref> In a press release following the committee's decision, Tuberville's campaign chairman Jordan Doufexis celebrated that "common sense has prevailed and this made-up 'residency' hoax will be put to bed for good."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Press |first=Coach Tuberville |date=2026-02-02 |title=ALGOP Unanimously Votes to Dismiss Ridiculous "Residency" Challenge Against Coach Tuberville |url=https://www.coachforgovernor.com/post/algop-unanimously-votes-to-dismiss-ridiculous-residency-challenge-against-coach-tuberville |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Coach Tommy Tuberville for Governor |language=en}}</ref> 

In March 2026, McFeeters announced on the steps of the [[Alabama State Capitol|Alabama Capitol]] that he had filed a lawsuit against Tuberville in the [[Covington County, Alabama|Covington County]] Circuit Court.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chapoco |first=Ralph |date=2026-03-24 |title=Republican gubernatorial candidate files lawsuit against U.S. Sen. Tommy Tuberville |url=https://alabamareflector.com/2026/03/24/republican-gubernatorial-candidate-files-lawsuit-against-u-s-sen-tommy-tuberville/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Reflector |language=en-US}}</ref> McFeeters, though not a lawyer, litigated the case ''[[Pro se legal representation in the United States|pro se]]'' and listed “God’s Law Team” as his law firm in the complaint.<ref>PLAINTIFF’S RESPONSE IN OPPOSITION TO DEFENDANT TUBERVILLE’S MOTION TO DISMISS AND MOTION FOR THRESHOLD DETERMINATION OF CONSTITUTIONAL ELIGIBILITY<nowiki/>https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/lagniappemobile.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/c/1e/c1e5cf02-ffb6-499b-a514-fd3140bd74ce/6a0c7e77a1d9f.pdf.pdf</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chapoco |first=Ralph |date=2026-03-24 |title=Republican gubernatorial candidate files lawsuit against U.S. Sen. Tommy Tuberville |url=https://alabamareflector.com/2026/03/24/republican-gubernatorial-candidate-files-lawsuit-against-u-s-sen-tommy-tuberville/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=Alabama Reflector |language=en-US}}</ref> McFeeters pledged that he would drop out of the race if Tuberville released records demonstrating proof of residency.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harrison |first=Claire |date=2026-03-25 |title=McFeeters files lawsuit challenging Tuberville’s residency |url=https://aldailynews.com/mcfeeters-files-lawsuit-challenging-tubervilles-residencyr/ |access-date=2026-07-15 |website=Alabama Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> Tuberville did not release any records, and the lawsuit was dismissed for improper venue on May 18, 2026, the day before the primary election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chapoco |first=Ralph |date=2026-05-20 |title=Judge dismisses lawsuit challenging Tommy Tuberville's eligibility to be governor |url=https://alabamareflector.com/2026/05/19/judge-dismisses-lawsuit-challenging-tommy-tubervilles-eligibility-to-be-governor/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Reflector |language=en-US}}</ref>

On May 27, 2026, the week after the primary election, McFeeters filed another challenge with the Alabama Republican Party, arguing that the party should void Tuberville's nomination on eligibility grounds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=JOHNSON |first=SCOTT |date=2026-05-27 |title=Candidate seeks to void Tuberville nomination |url=https://www.lagniappemobile.com/news/alabama/election_2026/candidate-seeks-to-void-tuberville-nomination/article_eeee2816-55e1-499c-88d1-e9994197cacd.html |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Lagniappe Daily |language=en}}</ref> The party's Candidate Committee voted to proceed with the contest, surprising McFeeters, who said he was "totally shocked."<ref>{{Cite web |last=JOHNSON |first=SCOTT |date=2026-06-01 |title=ALGOP advances Tuberville nomination challenge |url=https://www.lagniappemobile.com/news/alabama/algop-advances-tuberville-nomination-challenge/article_ce1da93a-071a-4c52-9cd5-d0fe5b246228.html |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Lagniappe Daily |language=en}}</ref> During the proceedings, Tuberville produced seven years of heavily redacted Alabama tax returns, from 2018 to 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barrett |first=Anna |date=2026-06-02 |title=Tuberville submits income tax returns, expert says it's not enough to prove residency |url=https://alabamareflector.com/2026/06/02/tuberville-submits-income-tax-returns-expert-says-its-not-enough-to-prove-residency/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Reflector |language=en-US}}</ref> However, by failing to adequately redact scannable [[PDF417|PDF417 barcodes]] in the corners of the document, the unredacted contents of the tax returns were inadvertently made available to the involved parties.<ref>{{Cite web |last=JOHNSON |first=SCOTT |date=2026-06-05 |title=Campaign exposes Tuberville’s tax, financial history |url=https://www.lagniappemobile.com/news/alabama/campaign-exposes-tuberville-s-tax-financial-history/article_578d2e17-d57a-4863-8682-3e3b65fe9a3a.html |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Lagniappe Daily |language=en}}</ref> McFeeters, unconvinced that the tax returns sufficiently demonstrated proof of residency, shared plans to continue his challenge, telling [[AL.com]], “I want his wife to tell me, with a straight face, that she lives in a one-bathroom house with her husband and adults and guests. A woman like that is not going to share a bathroom.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Ruth Serven |date=2026-06-02 |title=Tuberville releases long-awaited tax returns, says he’s lived in Alabama since 2018 |url=https://www.al.com/news/2026/06/tuberville-releases-long-awaited-tax-returns-says-hes-lived-in-alabama-since-2018.html |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=al |language=en}}</ref>

Following an internal closed-door hearing on June 14, 2026, the Alabama Republican Party Candidate Committee unanimously dismissed the challenge.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knowles |first=Sawyer |date=2026-06-15 |title=Alabama Republican Party rules that Tuberville fully meets residency requirements |url=https://256today.com/alabama-republican-party-rules-that-tuberville-fully-meets-residency-requirements/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=256 Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

In July 2026, McFeeters filed a second lawsuit with similar allegations in the [[Jefferson County, Alabama|Jefferson County]] Circuit Court.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shelley |first=Jonathan |date=July 30, 2026 |title=Back to court: Ken McFeeters sues (again) over Tuberville's residency, eligibility for governor |url=https://www.rocketcitynow.com/article/news/state/back-to-court-ken-mcfeeters-sues-again-over-tubervilles-residency-eligibility-for-governor/525-4cec25e8-bc59-4143-9721-479fa17644dc}}</ref> The case was dismissed on August 18, 2026 for lack of jurisdiction.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moon |first=Josh |date=2026-08-20 |title=Another Tuberville residency challenge has been dismissed |url=https://www.alreporter.com/2026/08/20/another-tuberville-residency-challenge-has-been-dismissed/ |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=Alabama Political Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref> On August 13, 2026, McFeeters additionally filed a federal lawsuit, which was dismissed one day later for lack of [[Standing (law)|standing]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shelley |first=Jonathan |date=August 14, 2026 |title=Judge dismisses federal lawsuit seeking to block Sen. Tuberville's run for governor |url=https://www.rocketcitynow.com/article/news/local/judge-dismisses-federal-lawsuit-seeking-to-block-sen-tubervilles-run-for-governor/525-dca50942-69d5-43d0-85b6-dc0f2678ce49}}</ref>

=== Quo warranto lawsuit ===
[[File:Barry Ragsdale - Anna Barrett, Alabama Reflector.jpg|thumb|219x219px|Birmingham lawyer Barry Ragsdale is an attorney for the plaintiffs.]]
On June 17, 2026, plaintiffs Brook Dorgan and Justin LeBlanc filed a lawsuit against Tuberville in the [[Montgomery County, Alabama|Montgomery County]] Circuit Court, which seeks a [[Quo warranto|writ of ''quo warranto'']] to invalidate Tuberville's candidacy. The complaint, citing voter registration records, tax records, campaign finance records, and quotes from Tuberville himself, alleges that Tuberville has not consistently maintained residence at his Auburn, Alabama property.<ref>{{Cite web |title=EXPEDITED COMPLAINT FOR QUO WARRANTO AND DECLARATORY RELIEF |url=https://whnt.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/06/Tuberville-Residency-Challenge-Lawsuit.pdf}}</ref> The complaint requested an expedited jury trial, with plaintiffs' attorney Barry Ragsdale saying on a podcast, "We think that your average person who sits on a jury is just never, ever going to believe the stories that Tuberville makes up about where he lives."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Barry Ragsdale on the Tuberville Lawsuit |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/barry-ragsdale-on-the-tuberville-lawsuit/id1845915473?i=1000774023089 |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Apple Podcasts |language=en-US}}</ref> Tuberville filed a motion to dismiss the suit on June 22, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harrison |first=Claire |date=2026-06-23 |title=Tuberville files motion to dismiss in latest residency case |url=https://aldailynews.com/tuberville-files-motion-to-dismiss-in-latest-residency-case/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> 

On July 9, 2026, Montgomery County Circuit Judge Brooke Reid dismissed the lawsuit for insufficient jurisdiction.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Barrett |first=Anna |date=2026-07-09 |title=Tommy Tuberville residency lawsuit dismissed by Montgomery judge |url=https://alabamareflector.com/2026/07/09/tommy-tuberville-residency-lawsuit-dismissed-by-montgomery-judge/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Alabama Reflector |language=en-US}}</ref> The dismissal order cites a lack of case law concerning whether ''quo warranto'' may be applied for party nominees. However, Reid did affirm that the state constitution allows the judiciary to determine whether an individual satisfies the "clearly set forth and unambiguous" requirements to hold office, which Tuberville's lawyers had disputed.<ref name=":1" /> Reid did not render a verdict on the underlying question of Tuberville's eligibility. 

On July 14, 2026, Ragsdale filed an appeal to the [[Supreme Court of Alabama|Alabama Supreme Court]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Barry Ragsdale appeals dismissed lawsuit challenging Tuberville’s… |url=https://1819news.com/news/item/barry-ragsdale-appeals-dismissed-lawsuit-challenging-tubervilles-residency-to-alabama-supreme-court |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[1819 News]] |language=en-US}}</ref>  The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal in a 7-0 ruling.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alabama Supreme Court rules 7-0 for Tuberville, ends ‘residency hoax’ in courts for good |url=https://yellowhammernews.com/alabama-supreme-court-rules-7-0-for-tuberville-ends-residency-hoax-in-courts-for-good/ |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=[[Yellowhammer News]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
